questions.problem:
Calculate the volume $V$ of the parallelepiped spanned by $x=⟨1,1,2⟩$, $y=⟨-3,2,0⟩$, and $z=⟨4,-2,1⟩.$

$V=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
The volume of the parallelepiped spanned by three vectors is given by the absolute value of their triple product.

First, we compute the triple product:

$$
\begin{aligned}x\cdot (y\times z) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 \\ -3 & 2 & 0 \\ 4 & -2 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & 0 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 0 \\ 4 & 1\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 2 \\ 4 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1(2\cdot 1-0\cdot (-2))-1((-3)\cdot 1-0\cdot 4)+2((-3)\cdot (-2)-2\cdot 4) \\  & =2+3-4 \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we take the absolute value. So, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped is 

$$
V=|1|=1.
$$

questions.problem: Find $k$ given that the vectors $a=⟨k,1,4⟩,$ $b=⟨8,0,3⟩,$ and $c=⟨3,1,1⟩$ are coplanar.
questions.worked_solution:
Computing the triple product, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =|\begin{aligned}k & 1 & 4 \\ 8 & 0 & 3 \\ 3 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k\cdot |\begin{aligned}0 & 3 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}8 & 3 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}|+4\cdot |\begin{aligned}8 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =k(0\cdot 1-1\cdot 3)-(8\cdot 1-3\cdot 3)+4(8\cdot 1-3\cdot 0) \\  & =-3k+1+32 \\  & =33-3k \\  & =3(11-k).\end{aligned}
$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}a\cdot (b\times c) & =0 \\ 3(11-k) & =0 \\ 11-k & =0 \\ k & =11\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $k=11.$

$$

$$

    

Three vectors are coplanar if and only if their triple product is zero:

$$
\begin{aligned}p\cdot (q\times r) & =0 \\ -3t-6 & =0 \\ -3t & =6 \\ t & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the three vectors are coplanar if and only if $t=-2.$

$V=${{field-1}}
questions.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(5j+5k)-(1j+3k) \\  & =4j+2k \\  & =⟨0,4,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(3i+4j+5k)-(1j+3k) \\  & =3i+3j+2k \\  & =⟨3,3,2⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(2i+2k)-(1j+3k) \\  & =2i-1j-1k \\  & =⟨2,-1,-1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}0 & 4 & 2 \\ 3 & 3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =0\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}|-4\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 2 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}|+2\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & 3 \\ 2 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-4(3\cdot -1-2\cdot 2)+2(3\cdot -1-3\cdot 2) \\  & =28-18 \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overset{\to }{AB},$ $\overset{\to }{AC},$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}$ is

$$
V=|10|=10.
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Calculate the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD},$ given the points $A(3,-1,2),$ $B(2,1,1),$ $C(-1,2,1),$ and $D(4,4,2).$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we find the displacement vectors $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ that span the parallelepiped:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =b-a \\  & =(2i+j+k)-(3i-j+2k) \\  & =-i+2j-k \\  & =⟨-1,2,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =c-a \\  & =(-i+2j+k)-(3i-j+2k) \\  & =-4i+3j-k \\  & =⟨-4,3,-1⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AD} & =d-a \\  & =(4i+4j+2k)-(3i-j+2k) \\  & =i+5j \\  & =⟨1,5,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to find the volume of the parallelepiped, we need to take the absolute value of the triple product of the above vectors.

Computing the triple product, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB}\cdot (\overset{\to }{AC}\times \overset{\to }{AD}) & =|\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & -1 \\ -4 & 3 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ 5 & 0\end{aligned}|-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}-4 & 3 \\ 1 & 5\end{aligned}| \\  & =-(3\cdot 0-5\cdot (-1))-2((-4)\cdot 0-1\cdot (-1))-((-4)\cdot 5-1\cdot 3) \\  & =-5-2+23 \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the volume of the corresponding parallelepiped spanned by $\overrightarrow{AB},$ $\overrightarrow{AC},$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}$ is

$$
V=|16|=16.
$$
